short: The design that finally combined firepower, protection and mobility in one tank.
full:
The A41 was designed from 1943 to deal with the Tiger and Panther, and six prototypes were shipped to Germany in May 1945 for trials, arriving after the fighting had stopped. It entered British service in December 1946 with the 5th Royal Tank Regiment. Successive marks moved from the 17-pounder to the 20-pounder and then to the 105 mm L7, a gun so good that the Americans, Germans and Israelis all adopted it.

The Centurion ended the British distinction between cruiser and infantry tanks and became the first of what would be called main battle tanks. Around 4,400 were built and sold to seventeen countries. It fought at the Imjin in Korea in 1951, in the Indo-Pakistani wars, and with Israel on the Golan Heights in 1967 and 1973. British gun tanks gave way to the Chieftain from 1966, but the Centurion AVRE served with the Royal Engineers through the 1991 Gulf War and was retired in 1992.
